edges.notes: Unit files are the primary declarative input interpreted by the systemd service manager suite.
Unit directives map to cgroups, namespaces, and capability policy enforced with Linux kernel facilities.
Boot loader entries and targets coordinate with systemd target units on typical images.
UKI-based boots still use standard unit/target activation after init.
Container images may ship systemd units for in-container service supervision when used.
Linux nodes commonly run kubelet, container runtime, and node agents as systemd-managed unit files.
Portable service images include unit files interpreted under the same systemd unit model after attach.
Merged system extensions can include unit files and drop-ins under standard unit paths after sysext merge.
Merged configuration extensions can supply unit drop-ins and daemon config under /etc after confext merge.
Debian services on default systemd installs are expressed as unit files under the standard systemd unit model.
Ubuntu services on default systemd installs are expressed as unit files under the standard systemd unit model.
Fedora services on default systemd installs are expressed as unit files under the standard systemd unit model.
RHEL services on default systemd installs are expressed as unit files under the standard systemd unit model.
Rocky Linux services on default systemd installs are expressed as unit files under the standard systemd unit model.
AlmaLinux services on default systemd installs are expressed as unit files under the standard systemd unit model.
CentOS Stream services on default systemd installs are expressed as unit files under the standard systemd unit model.
Historical CentOS Linux services on default systemd installs were expressed as unit files under the standard systemd unit model where systemd applied.
